question.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{5}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{5}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{5}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{5}}{(\sqrt{5})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{5}}{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the product rule to simplify the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{5}}{5} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3\cdot 5}}{5} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{15}}{5} & \end{aligned}
$$
